name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Security Controls
description: Security and privacy controls for federal and enterprise information systems.

rules.title: SQL Input Validation and Sanitization
rules.summary: The information system checks the validity of information inputs to prevent SQL injection.
rules.description: Information input validation ensures inputs are verified against valid syntax and constraints.

rules.title: Command Input Validation
rules.summary: The information system validates inputs passed to system commands to prevent command injection.
rules.description: Prevents arbitrary command execution on host operating systems.

rules.title: File Path Input Validation
rules.summary: The information system validates path inputs to enforce access control boundaries.
rules.description: Validates that path references remain within authorized storage boundaries.

rules.title: FIPS-Compliant Cryptographic Ciphers
rules.summary: The information system implements approved cryptographic modules and key lengths (FIPS 140-3).
rules.description: Deprecated algorithms like DES and RC4 violate federal cryptographic standards.

rules.control: SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest
rules.title: Strong Cryptographic Hashing at Rest
rules.summary: The information system protects the integrity and confidentiality of information at rest using strong hashes.
rules.description: Broken hashes like MD5 must not be used for data integrity verification.
